quotes.text: You're not buying agriculture — you're buying legitimate nothing.
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: Cult-ish year-three usage is the single best metric in this category.
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: If those two clear… buy the nothing.
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: 'Buy the nothing.' Put that on the gate, ma.
quotes.author: — Vikram

chatMessages.text: Riya, confession — we rented Ashok's farm six weekends to 'test the dream,' and you know what we did? Two hours of gardening, and six hours of absolutely nothing under a tree.

That IS the data, you two. You're not buying agriculture — you're buying legitimate nothing. So the cottage budget shrinks, the operator quality rises, and the one question becomes: what exactly do you own? Title, structure, exit. Trees can come later.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “The persuasive channel was reels; the corrective channel was a rented weekend. They didn't ask me for the best farm — they asked me what they would actually own, in structure, before any trees. That single question, plus a calendar audit that scared them, is why they bought a half-acre they'll likely never regret: it was bought as nothing, not as an asset.”

beforeItems.text: Buying farmland is buying a sensible second asset
We'll drive out whenever we feel like it — roughly every weekend
The best-reeling operator with the prettiest year-three photos wins
If we buy land, the water and the trees mostly look after themselves

afterItems.text: A farm is a lifestyle purchase, not an investment — and they admitted which one it was
11 real free weekends drive the usage forecast, not the imagined 24
Operator track record and borewell records beat gate designs every time
Water in August is a person you can name, not a management fee you can delegate
